title: Once a Year, Once for All

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "This is to be a lasting ordinance for you: Atonement is to be made once a year for all the sins of the Israelites." And it was done, as the LORD commanded Moses. - Lev 16:34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once a year. Every year. Again and again, for as long as the tabernacle stood.

That repetition was the great limitation, and Hebrews names it plainly: those sacrifices are an annual reminder of sins, because it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins (Heb 10:3-4). Every Day of Atonement both dealt with sin and reminded Israel that it was not finished. Next year they would be back.

Then, on a Friday afternoon outside Jerusalem, Jesus said three words: It is finished (John 19:30).

And at that moment the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom (Matt 27:51). Torn from the top — no human hand did it. The way into the Most Holy Place, closed for fifteen centuries except for one man on one day, was opened permanently.

We do not have a Day of Atonement. We have an atonement that never needs repeating. He did not enter by means of the blood of goats and calves; but he entered the Most Holy Place once for all by his own blood (Heb 9:12).

Once for all. Not once a year.

The final line of the chapter says it was done, as the LORD commanded Moses. And centuries later, everything it pointed to was also done.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you live as though your forgiveness needs renewing, or is finished?
2. What does the torn curtain mean for your prayers today?
3. How has this chapter deepened your understanding of the cross?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You entered once for all with Your own blood and tore the curtain open. Nothing remains to be paid. Let me live in the freedom of "it is finished." Amen.
